overview.text: Southern California Public Power Authority (SCPPA), on behalf of its Member utilities, solicits proposals for renewable energy projects or products, optionally with co-located energy storage, for commercial operation or delivery starting in 2025 and beyond. Structures may be SCPPA ownership or a power purchase agreement with or without an ownership option. Rolling RFP issued February 14, 2025; proposals due June 30, 2025.

summary.issuing_organization: Southern California Public Power Authority (SCPPA), acting for its Member utilities; Q1/Q2 2025 Renewable Energy Resources and Energy Storage Solutions RFP; contact renewablesrfp@scppa.org; reference number not specified in the document

scope.text: Renewable energy projects or products under the California RPS programs, with commercial operation or delivery starting in 2025 and beyond.
Accepted structures: SCPPA project ownership, a PPA with an ownership option, or a PPA without an ownership option.

Eligible resources include wind, geothermal, biomass, biomethane, hydro, solar, solar thermal, waste-to-energy, renewable fuel cells, permanent load shifting, hydrogen, flexible and hybrid projects, and unbundled RECs.
Energy storage may be proposed only combined with a renewable energy project.
Portfolio Content Category 2 and 3 REC-only proposals are also considered, for any term.
Delivery term: minimum is 1 month with no maximum; both short-term and long-term (greater than 10 years) delivery sought.
Delivery at the listed points of delivery (CAISO Grid with preference of SP15, among others) or other points if all transmission, ancillary and scheduling costs are included.
Out of scope: stand-alone energy storage, to be proposed under SCPPA's separate Standalone Energy Storage RFP.

key_requirements.text: Proposal must be signed by an officer authorized to bind the Respondent, with the non-collusion declaration in the transmittal letter.
Only proven renewable technologies; experimental or speculative proposals will not be entertained.
Facility must be RPS compliant and compliant with the California Energy Commission emissions performance standard (EPS) upon COD and throughout the term.
Seller must assume the risk of bringing the facility back into RPS or EPS compliance if a change in law makes it noncompliant.
Energy storage paired with a renewable project must have capacity of at least one half the total interconnection capacity offered and a duration of at least 4 hours.
Respondent must handle site control (SCPPA must be allowed to assume or cure any default in site control documents) and bears environmental liability, hazardous materials and removal.
Respondent must obtain all construction, operational and environmental permits and licenses, and construction financing.
SCPPA must receive all environmental attributes and all capacity rights associated with the project.
Project must be certified RPS-eligible by the California Energy Commission no later than 6 months after COD and registered in WREGIS no later than 3 months before COD.
If a SCPPA Member is in the EIM, acceptance into the Energy Imbalance Market is required before any test energy; Seller must give technical design data at least nine months before test energy.

eligibility.text: Minimum turnover, years of experience, number of similar projects and certifications: Not specified in the document

Must provide current financial statements of all entities involved: audited statements not more than twelve months old, annual reports, FERC Form 1; otherwise verifiable statements for the past three (3) years and Dun & Bradstreet number where available.
Must identify project participants and key personnel with their qualifications and experience on similar projects, and give a commitment statement for retaining them.
Must list existing projects in commercial operation and references for similar completed projects, with contact person, phone number and address.
Must disclose any service rendered to SCPPA or its Members within the last five (5) years, or else give references over that period.
Must address possible conflicts of interest with SCPPA and Members, including lawsuits; these do not automatically disqualify.
Must indicate all pending litigation that could affect the proposal, existing contracts, operation or financial stability.
Must not offer gifts or promises of remuneration to SCPPA or Member officials or staff, and must not collude with other respondents.

important_dates.text: RFP issued February 14, 2025; RFP open period February 14, 2025-June 30, 2025 (rolling RFP).
Responses to clarification questions: 5 Business Days after submitted.
Proposals due on or before 12:00 PM PPT on June 30, 2025.
Review of proposals: 5 Business Days after submittal, during the RFP open period.
Selection of Respondent(s): from submittal date to no later than June 30, 2025.
Proposal validity: twelve (12) months from the Proposals Due date, unless the Respondent states a shorter term.
Bid opening date: Not specified in the document

commercial_requirements.text: Fixed energy price (preferred): nominal $/MWh as of the year of COD, no escalation, covering energy, capacity, RECs and all other products.
Alternative: variable index energy price plus fixed capacity/REC price in nominal $/MWh with no escalation; preferred by some Member utilities.
Storage price must be quoted in addition to the energy price, in $/MWh and in $/kW-month for a minimum of 4-hour systems; include a Solar-Only price if solar and BESS are proposed.
Any price increase after proposal submittal could end negotiations and prompt reevaluation of the proposal.
Transmission cost to the delivery point must be in the energy price; CAISO delivery must include a $/MWh price adder fixed for the contract term.
Ownership offer must state a purchase price at COD in $/kW plus recurring owner costs; PPA with purchase option must give a buyout price or formula and an energy price without buyout.
Performance Assurance amounts in nominal dollars must be stated, through COD and after COD as a Letter of Credit; SCPPA may require performance security before negotiations.
Not specified in the document: EMD or bid security, tender fee, payment terms, liquidated damages and warranty

project_duration.text: Delivery term: minimum of 1 month with no maximum; PPA terms up to the life of the facility will be considered.
Contract duration and award date: Not specified in the document
Respondent must propose COD and a major milestone schedule through construction, test energy and COD.

important_conditions.text: Evaluation: initial screening eliminates proposals that are non-responsive, miss minimum requirements, are not economically competitive, or come from Respondents lacking creditworthiness or financial resources.
Evaluation: each Member Agency applies its own criteria, which may include price, size, location, schedule, COD, viability, guarantees and fit with its resource plan.
Evaluation: scoring weights and minimum score: Not specified in the document
Evaluation: project evaluations include the full cost of delivery to customers of Member Agencies in Southern California.
Submission: one electronic copy must be emailed to renewablesrfp@scppa.org by 12:00PM (PPT) on June 30, 2025; one hard copy is optional, to Glendora, California.

Submission: proposal must include all Section V required elements (transmittal letter, respondent information, renewable category, project details, experience, references, conflicts); SCPPA may disqualify one that does not.
Submission: Term Sheet (Appendix A) must be completed, and the ESS Specifications (Appendix B) for storage within LADWP's Balancing Authority; both are posted as separate documents.
Submission: must identify proprietary material exempt from the Public Records Act, or exemption is waived.
Risk: SCPPA may award irrespective of price or technical ability, reject all proposals for any reason, and proposers have no legal recourse.
Risk: schedule is subject to change, interviews are TBD, and SCPPA may start negotiations and sign agreements before the proposal deadline.
Risk: Seller bears the risk of RPS or EPS noncompliance from a change in law for the PPA term.
Risk: all contact with SCPPA Board, staff or Members on this RFP, outside the specified method, is prohibited until contract execution and may mean immediate disqualification.
Risk: CEQA compliance is required before SCPPA can execute an agreement, and test energy before COD is curtailable at any time without compensation.
Risk: listing protectable documents obliges the Respondent to indemnify and defend SCPPA against disclosure claims.
